_note: The catalog of OPTIONAL outside tools the kit suggests (read by tools/suggest.mjs and tools/tips.mjs). The kit works on its own code without any of them. detect = existence checks only (a command on PATH, an app path, a non-empty key FILE, an MCP server name): keys are never read, nothing goes over the network. No prices and no plan claims here: the user checks each site.
baseline: a free built-in voice (your computer's own speech engine; basic quality, no account), so a whole reel can be made with no outside tool
scripts, hooks and captions, fact checks and the Gate A, B and C approvals
animated reels drawn from code in every style (print, depth, talking and the scene styles), rendered on your own computer
the built-in cover from your brand template, the on-screen text checks and the final-file checks
the content calendar, the dashboard and the analytics read-outs from your own numbers

categories.title: Voice
categories.question: Do you have a voice service for the voice-over?

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.what_you_get: A natural, steady voice-over for the whole reel, in a voice you pick or your own recorded voice, instead of the free built-in voice (your computer's own speech engine, basic quality).
tools.example: a natural voice for the whole reel instead of the built-in basic voice
connect: Check the site for the current plan and licence terms, and that your plan allows commercial use. A cloned voice must be your own, or you need written permission.
Claude makes the empty file ~/.config/bagelunit-reels/elevenlabs.key and opens it (SETUP.md section 3).
You paste the key into that file yourself and save it. Never paste it into the chat.
Run kit checkup to confirm the kit finds it (it tests the key and never shows it).

tip_lines.voice: could give this reel a natural voice instead of the built-in basic voice

tools.name: Another voice service
tools.what_you_get: Any other text-to-speech service (Azure, Google, Amazon Polly, OpenAI, a local model) or your own recording as the reel's voice.
tools.example: a take you recorded yourself, or an export from a voice tool you already pay for
connect: Check the service's terms for commercial use.

Put a tiny script around the service's API (its key stays in the script's own environment, never in the kit), then set brand/brand.json voice to {"provider": "command", "command": "python3 /path/my-tts.py --in {text_file} --out {audio_file}"}. The command must write an audio file to the second path. A wrapper example is in docs/sound.md, section 'The voice itself'.
Or record the voice yourself and drop the audio file in the reel folder as the kit's voice step describes (studio/KIT.md, own recordings).

categories.title: Music and sound effects
categories.question: Do you have a music or sound-effects library?

tools.name: Uppbeat
tools.what_you_get: Licensed music beds you download by hand and record in the kit with their licence.
tools.example: a music bed that ducks under your voice, recorded with its licence
connect: Check the site for what your plan covers and the credit line it asks for on the channel you post on.
Download the track from the site (there is no API).
Record it with kit licensed add <file> --type music --title "..." --artist "..." --url ... so its licence and credit are kept (see /licensed-assets).

tip_lines.sound: could supply a licensed music bed that ducks under your voice, recorded with its licence
tip_lines.export: could supply a licensed music bed for this reel, recorded with its licence

tools.name: Epidemic Sound
tools.what_you_get: Licensed music and sound effects, searchable from Claude if you have its connector.
tools.example: a search for a calm 40-second track and a door-slam effect, both recorded with their licence
connect: Check the site for what your plan covers for the channel you post on.
Add the Epidemic Sound connector in Claude (Settings, Connectors) and sign in yourself.
Search and download through it, then record each file with kit licensed add (see /licensed-assets).

tip_lines.sound: could supply licensed music and effects you can search from Claude
tip_lines.export: could supply licensed music and effects you can search from Claude

tools.name: Blender (with the Blender Lab MCP)
tools.what_you_get: Real 3D shots rendered on your own computer: a product, a label, a phone mock-up, a 3D title or a map as a short clip or a still. The MCP lets Claude open a .blend and look at it; the kit's scripts do not need it.
tools.example: a 3D product shot or a shaded-relief terrain map
connect: Blender is free from blender.org. Install it the usual way for your system.
Run kit checkup, or ask Claude to run /blender-shot: the kit renders from the command line.
Optional: add the Blender Lab MCP so Claude can open a .blend and take screenshots (Blender's own docs have the steps; check them for the current ones).
Models, textures and fonts you bring in carry their own licences: keep them in your brand folder.

tip_lines.start: could add a 3D product shot or a shaded-relief terrain map to this reel
tip_lines.cover: could render a 3D still for this cover
tip_lines.render: could add a 3D shot or a terrain map (/blender-shot)

categories.title: Generated video
categories.question: Do you have a generated-video tool?

tools.name: Higgsfield
tools.what_you_get: Short generated shots or stills for atmosphere you cannot film, always labelled on screen and never carrying the claim.
tools.example: a 5 second establishing shot of a 1900s factory floor, labelled Re-creation
connect: Check the site for its current plan, credits and commercial-use terms. The kit never starts a paid generation without your yes to that exact job.
Add the Higgsfield connector in Claude (Settings, Connectors) and sign in yourself, or make the shot on the site and download it.
Record the file with kit licensed add <file> --type generated-video --tool "Higgsfield" (see /generated-shots). Label it on screen as a re-creation.

tip_lines.start: could make a short labelled re-creation shot for this reel (/generated-shots)

tools.name: Another generated-video tool
tools.what_you_get: Any other generator: download the clip and the kit records it the same way, with its tool and label.
tools.example: a short atmosphere clip from the generator you already use, recorded and labelled
connect: Make the shot in that tool and check its terms for commercial use.
Record it with kit licensed add <file> --type generated-video --tool "<name>" (see /generated-shots).

categories.title: Design

tip_lines.cover: could make a cover or background picture

tools.name: Adobe connector for Claude
tools.what_you_get: Lets Claude work in your Adobe apps for you, if you have it.

connect: Check the site for which Adobe plan the connector needs.

categories.title: Research and competitors
categories.question: Do you have a research or scraping tool?

tools.name: Apify
tools.what_you_get: Competitor tracking beyond what Meta's API shows: other accounts' recent reels with views, likes and comments, personal accounts included. /account-audit and the dashboard's competitors section read it. You pay Apify as you go: the kit shows the estimated cost first, logs it, and runs nothing unless brand.json autopilot.scrape is true.
tools.example: /account-audit on five rival accounts: the reels that beat each account's own median (the 3x rule), shown on the dashboard with post ideas
connect: Make an Apify account and check the site for the current plan, free credit and usage terms.
Create an API token at console.apify.com/settings/integrations (Claude can open the page with the browser tool; you copy the token yourself).
Save it alone on one line in ~/.config/bagelunit-reels/apify.key (Claude makes the empty file and opens it for you; never paste the token into the chat).
Set brand.json autopilot.scrape to true (that is your yes), then run /account-audit or /content-calendar competitors --apify; the kit prints the cost first.
